$comment: Project-wide guard rails, checked in so they apply to every agent and every session.
The playtest tooling writes directly to a database, and live and staging share one
Firebase project and one storage bucket. dev/scripts/playtest/lib/dbGuard.js makes that
tooling structurally incapable of naming a live collection. These rules close the way
around it: the CLIs that can reach the live data without going through Node at all.
These are denials for the assistant, not for the developer. Any of them remains
available by running it yourself in a terminal, which is the point — an irreversible
operation on production data should be a deliberate human act.
The allowances below are the opposite case: this repository's own scripts, run against
the local machine alone. Writing a dev-log post means booting a local dev server and
taking dozens of screenshots against it, one capture run at a time, and every one of
those was a permission prompt for something that reaches nothing outside this checkout
and no database but the Firebase emulator. Note that they widen nothing the deny list
closes: a rule in "deny" always outranks one in "allow".
The release-train workflow adds three more groups, on the same principle — everything
that only observes is allowed, and everything that changes something outside this
checkout still asks:
- Reading the repository and CI (git status/log/diff/show/rev-parse, gh run/workflow
view). `git add` is here too, since staging a file is undone by unstaging it.
`git commit` and `git push` are deliberately absent: pushing to main deploys.
- Building and testing locally. These are slow, not dangerous.
- `dev/scripts/vps/maintenance.js audit` and the two --dry-run forms. The audit's
command set is fixed and reads only; the dry runs report what they would change and
change nothing. `reclaim --apply` and `upgrade --apply` are not here, and neither is
a general `ssh` allowance — that VPS runs live as well as staging, so an unprompted
root shell on it is an unprompted root shell on production. Anything the audit does
not already answer is worth one prompt.
The deny additions close the two levers that move production: the Promote to Live and
Rollback Live workflows. No automated run has any business dispatching those.
